title: AnyWork — Your local agents. Anywhere.
description: Continue local Codex and DeepSeek Harness work from a browser or Android phone. Conversations, approvals, files and tools, connected to your own computer.
release: Open source. Runs on your computer.
headline:
Good work.
No fixed address.
intro: Let your agents keep working on your computer. Sign in from a browser or phone, find your computer, and continue the conversation, approvals and work.
demoLabel: The conversation. And everything around it.

manifestoText: Pick up an existing chat, follow tool calls and subagents, review files, and keep the conversation moving. Connect to Codex or the official shared Harness host.
feature1Text: Stream replies, find earlier messages, steer running work and keep drafts between chats. Tools and subagents have their own place in the conversation.
feature2Text: Respond to an approval, inspect a change, or add an image with your own annotations. Browser notifications bring you back when the work needs attention.
feature3Text: Open files, documents, Git changes and a terminal beside your conversation. Each chat remembers its own set of tabs.
connectText: Find a device through your account, confirm its identity, then establish an encrypted connection. Only your two devices decrypt your work. Cloud services handle identity and required connection information. Advanced routes below retain manual access.
lanText: Connect directly on a trusted LAN. Your device reaches the service running on your own computer.
tunnelText: Use a temporary Cloudflare address or configure your own domain. Temporary addresses can change when the tunnel restarts.
vpnText: Connect Android through your private WireGuard network, or configure a compatible TLS relay. Bring your own network or relay.
routeFoot: No mandatory AnyWork cloud relay. Model requests still go to your configured model provider. Third-party tunnels follow their own policies.
startTitle: From your desk to your pocket, in three steps.
step1Text: Install AnyWork on your Mac and connect your existing local agents. Other platforms retain advanced manual connections.
step2Text: Sign in on the computer and explicitly allow access from your other devices.
step3Text: Use the same account on your phone or browser, choose your device, and continue over an encrypted connection.
downloadText: Install the manager on your computer. Take the workspace with you.

faq1Q: Does the work run on my phone?
faq1A: No. Your agent and tools run on your host computer. Your phone or browser connects to that workspace. The host needs to stay awake and connected.
faq2Q: Can I continue an existing chat?
faq2A: Yes. Codex desktop sharing depends on compatible Unix interfaces and the installed version; Windows uses CLI-backed chats. Harness connects to the original official 0.2.2-rc.1 Web/Desktop host, preserving native session identity and history. Its discovery companion provides the host address; a TUI without a shared carrier cannot be controlled.
faq3Q: Where do my account and work data live?
faq3A: Logto manages your account and minimal device settings. CyberGrid exchanges connection information. Conversations, files, terminal content and private device keys stay on your devices. Account access requires local sign-in and authorization; advanced manual connections remain available.
faq4Q: What is included in this release?
faq4A: Codex and the official shared Harness host are supported. Harness goal/plan, fork and message editing are not included. Full Codex goal operations need a compatible shared engine; the desktop follower can read and pause goals. Voice, cross-client native queue migration and closed-browser push are not included.
footerLegal: Independent open-source project. Not affiliated with OpenAI. Codex is a trademark of its owner.
privacy: No analytics tracking or session replay. Logto and CyberGrid process account and required connection metadata.
